metadata.note: The Canada Southern ('CASO') was the New York Central system's Ontario short cut: a flat, straight, 229-mile line across the base of the Ontario peninsula that let Michigan Central trains run Detroit-Buffalo without touching the congested Great Western or Grand Trunk. Chartered Feb 28 1868 as the Erie and Niagara Extension Railway and renamed the Canada Southern Railway Dec 24 1869, it opened between St. Thomas and Amherstburg on the Detroit River in 1872 and was completed east to Fort Erie on the Niagara River by early 1873. Cornelius Vanderbilt took control Jan 1 1876; the Michigan Central leased the whole line for 99 years from Jan 1 1883, and the New York Central subleased it in 1929. Until the Detroit River Tunnel opened in 1910 the western end depended on car ferries across the Detroit River. Everything the map already shows for the Michigan Central (michigan_central_detroit_chicago.geojson) fed into this line: without the CASO the NYC's Detroit-Buffalo trains had no route of their own. Penn Central held it 1968-1976 and Conrail 1976-1985, before CN and CP bought it jointly on Apr 30 1985; the line through Niagara Falls was shut and lifted in 2001, and most of the route west of St. Thomas is now abandoned. COLOR SPLIT 2026-08-24: per the same-company-same-color rule, feature(s) whose ownership passed to the New York Central were split at the documented transfer date into a pre-NYC feature (original company color) and an NYC-colored feature (matching new_york_central.geojson's canonical color), sharing identical geometry, rather than coloring the whole multi-era line with the original company's color throughout.

metadata.niagara_branch_geometry_note: Niagara branch re-traced from OpenStreetMap 2026-08-24. The previous 13-point version was unusable: it began at a Welland city anchor lying on no track, jumped 17 km northeast, scribbled around Niagara Falls and ended on a Niagara Falls anchor 4.8 km off the end of the trace. It now runs from the junction with the CASO main line just east of Welland, northeast along the abandoned branch alignment (OSM ways 533196150, 533196149, 40636798, 533196148, 27034213) to the surviving portion still in service as the CPKC Montrose Spur, then north through Montrose on abandoned right of way to the Canadian abutment of the Michigan Central bridge at the Whirlpool Rapids, and across the bridge itself (OSM way 53192312) to the New York shore. Traced length 21.9 km.
metadata.freight_only_audit: 2026-08-24: removed as part of a repo-wide freight-only audit. Removed here: segment 1968-1985 from caso-main-amherstburg-fort-erie (Penn Central/Conrail freight only after passenger decline); segment 1985-2001 from caso-main-amherstburg-fort-erie (CN/CP ownership and rundown; no passenger service claimed); segment 1968-2001 from caso-niagara-branch (Penn Central, Conrail then CN/CP freight only); segment 1968-1985 from caso-detroit-river-tunnel (Penn Central/Conrail freight; tunnel remains freight-only today). REPO RULE: this map shows PASSENGER rail only. Freight-only operation is not represented -- a line's segments must end when its passenger service ends. See CONVENTIONS.md.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
